name: Alexander Rodchenko
bio: A Russian artist, sculptor, photographer, and graphic designer. He was one of the founders of constructivism and Russian design. He rejected artistic expression for objective reality, using radical viewpoints to shake up the viewer's perception.

name: Henri Cartier-Bresson
bio: A French artist and humanist photographer considered a master of candid photography. He pioneered the genre of street photography and viewed his craft as 'the decisive moment'—capturing an event's essence in a fleeting fraction of a second.

name: Andreas Gursky
bio: A German photographer known for his large-format, digitally-manipulated color photographs. His work often depicts subjects of global commerce and contemporary life, such as stock exchanges, factories, and crowds, viewed from a distanced, objective perspective.

name: Andy Warhol
bio: An American artist who was a leading figure in the visual art movement known as pop art. His photography was integral to his process, using Polaroid cameras to capture subjects for his famous silkscreen paintings and producing a vast archive of social documentation.

name: Dorothea Lange
bio: An American documentary photographer and photojournalist, best known for her Depression-era work for the Farm Security Administration. Her photographs humanized the consequences of the Great Depression and profoundly influenced the development of documentary photography.

name: Edward Burtynsky
bio: A Canadian photographer and artist known for his large-format photographs of industrial landscapes—mines, quarries, dams, and factories. His work explores the impact of human industry on the planet, blending art with environmental activism.

name: Elliott Erwitt
bio: An American photographer known for his black-and-white candid photographs of ironic and absurd situations in everyday life. A member of Magnum Photos since 1953, he was also a prolific commercial photographer and filmmaker.

name: Ernst Haas
bio: An Austrian photographer and pioneer of color photography. He was a master of using color to create poetic, evocative images. He is famous for his photo essays on cities, nature, and for his iconic images of New York.

name: Eve Arnold
bio: An American photojournalist, best known for her portrait of Marilyn Monroe and her work on the film 'The Misfits'. She was the first female photographer to join Magnum Photos in 1957 and documented a wide range of subjects, from celebrities to marginalized communities.

name: Gillian Wearing
bio: A British conceptual artist and photographer who won the Turner Prize in 1997. Her work often involves people from the public, using photography and video to explore identity, confession, and the relationship between the public and private self.

name: Gregory Crewdson
bio: An American photographer known for elaborately staged, cinematic photographs that depict eerie, melancholic scenes of American suburban life. His images are produced on a large scale, resembling film stills and exploring the psychology of everyday moments.

name: Ian Berry
bio: A British photojournalist, best known for his documentation of the apartheid regime in South Africa. He covered the Soweto uprising and other key moments in the anti-apartheid movement, and has worked extensively for The Observer and Magnum Photos.

name: Jeff Wall
bio: A Canadian artist known for his large-scale, back-lit color photographs. He creates meticulously staged tableaux that often reference art history, literature, and contemporary social issues, pioneering the 'cinematographic' approach to fine art photography.

name: Julia Margaret Cameron
bio: A British photographer who is considered one of the most important portraitists of the 19th century. Known for her soft-focus, close-up portraits of famous Victorians, she used her camera to create art, often depicting religious or literary scenes.

name: Nadar (Gaspard-Félix Tournachon)
bio: A French photographer, caricaturist, journalist, and balloonist. He is famous for his pioneering aerial photographs from a hot-air balloon and for his studio portraits of the Parisian intelligentsia, breaking conventions with his use of dramatic lighting.

name: Richard Drew
bio: An American photojournalist for the Associated Press, most famous for his iconic photograph 'The Falling Man' taken during the September 11 attacks in 2001. He has also covered major events like the Vietnam War and the Rodney King riots.

name: Robert Doisneau
bio: A French photographer who, along with Henri Cartier-Bresson, was a pioneer of photojournalism and street photography in France. He is known for his tender, often humorous depictions of everyday Parisian life, including his famous image 'The Kiss by the Hôtel de Ville'.

name: Slim Aarons
bio: An American photographer who documented the leisure and lifestyles of the rich and famous, particularly in the mid-20th century. His work is known for its sun-drenched aesthetic and captures of the high society at play.

name: Steve McCurry
bio: An American photojournalist best known for his evocative, colorful photographs of the world's conflicts and cultures. His most famous image is the 'Afghan Girl' (Sharbat Gula) taken in a refugee camp in Pakistan in 1984.

name: Thomas Struth
bio: A German photographer who is a prominent member of the Düsseldorf School. He is known for his large-scale, meticulously composed images of cityscapes, architecture, museum interiors, portraits, and family groups, often exploring the relationship between people and their cultural environments.

name: William Anders
bio: An American astronaut, engineer, and photographer. A member of the Apollo 8 crew, he took the iconic 'Earthrise' photograph on Christmas Eve 1968, showing the Earth rising over the lunar surface. It became one of the most influential images in environmental history.
